claims.text: Replacing conventional EAM references with a machine-learning interatomic potential trained on ab initio solid and liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in high-temperature high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid high-entropy-alloy states near melting.
The relevant high-temperature solid states are ordered, while the liquid states are disordered.
The proposed intervention is to train a neural-network or Gaussian-approximation potential on diverse configurations sampled by ab initio molecular dynamics in both liquid and solid phases.
The method is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing four to six principal elements.
NbMoTaW is a relevant refractory high-entropy-alloy example with a high melting point.
CoCrFeMnNi is a relevant 3d-transition-metal high-entropy-alloy example with temperature-dependent solid-phase behavior.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.8–1.0 times the alloy melting temperature.
Machine-learning local-environment descriptors can represent the multiple atomic configurations encountered in the liquid alloy.
Training on a comprehensive set of high-temperature liquid environments will make the machine-learning reference distribution more closely match the ab initio target distribution.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more robust free-energy estimates.
The machine-learning reference will improve convergence and decrease integration-path length relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The machine-learning reference is expected to improve phase-space overlap by more than a factor of two.
TOR-TILD's conventional EAM references inadequately span the diverse atomic configurations of the liquid state.
Applicability to low-temperature ordered phases or alloys with substantially different bonding character is uncertain.
The magnitude of improvement depends on training-set completeness and the machine-learning model used.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement, operationalized as at least a twofold reduction in path mismatch or corresponding convergence improvement relative to EAM under identical conditions, would falsify the hypothesis.
